snap.text: You meant to say it calmly. It came out at a volume that set off a car alarm. Their lip wobbles. Yours does too.

styles.title: The Tag-Teamer
styles.text: You passed the baton. Sometimes it was a relay. Sometimes it was a hot potato. Either way, two of you ran the race.

styles.title: The Negotiator
styles.text: Every snack was a treaty. Every shoe was a summit. You'd be terrifying at a car dealership.

styles.title: The Screen Diplomat
styles.text: A man in corduroy did a lot of your parenting this week. He did it well. You'll deal with the screen-off meltdowns later. You always do.

styles.title: The Martyr
styles.text: You did everything yourself, perfectly, and told no one. Your partner is still not sure what you did all week. Neither is your spine.

styles.title: The Bribe Economist
styles.text: Crackers, stickers, one more episode. The toddler has learned the value of a deal, and the deal has gotten expensive.

styles.title: The Drill Sergeant
styles.text: No meant no. No meant no forty times. The tantrums were loud, but they were short, and they knew where they stood.

modifiers.title: Monday
modifiers.text: Back to it. The weekend was a beautiful lie.

modifiers.title: Work Deadline
modifiers.text: The report is due at 5. Your toddler is due at everything else.

modifiers.title: Daycare Closed: Pink Eye
modifiers.text: Pink eye at daycare. Your toddler is fine. Your toddler is also home all day, touching every surface in the house with intent.

modifiers.title: Date Night
modifiers.text: The sitter arrives at 7:00. The reservation is at 7:30. All you have to do is get through the day with enough left to put on real pants.

modifiers.title: Teething
modifiers.text: A molar is coming in. Your toddler is chewing everything, including grudges.

modifiers.title: Grandma Is Visiting
modifiers.text: Free childcare! Also opinions. So many opinions.

modifiers.title: Potty Training: Day 3
modifiers.text: The internet said it would take three days. It is day 3. The internet lied.

modifiers.title: Sleep Regression
modifiers.text: Your toddler did stand-up comedy from 2 to 4 AM. You slept in installments.

tasks.label: Call the pediatrician about the rash

lifeline.title: Grandma to the Rescue
lifeline.text: You call your mother. She arrives in eleven minutes with a casserole, a bag of cookies and a list of observations. She sends you to bed at 4 PM. You don't argue.

collapse.title: Parent.exe Has Stopped Responding
collapse.text: You sat down on the kitchen floor to tie a shoe and simply did not get up again. Your toddler covers you with a dish towel and says, "Night night." Your partner finds you like that at 6.

talk.title: We Need to Talk
talk.text: Not a fight, exactly. Two people at the kitchen counter, too tired to finish their sentences. The monitor hisses. Neither of you moves. Next week, you'll try the ledger thing.

ballpit.title: The House Has Fallen
ballpit.text: Your home is now an installation. A local gallery calls it "a bold statement on domestic entropy." The couch is under there somewhere.

groupchat.title: Removed From the Group Chat
groupchat.text: "Admin removed you." Three words, forty-one parents. You'll never know when pajama day is again. Your toddler, unaware of your social death, hands you a rock.

sitter_quits.title: The Sitter Quits at the Door
sitter_quits.text: The sitter rings the bell at 7:00. Your toddler answers it, naked, holding a spatula, wide awake. The sitter looks at you, looks at the spatula, and leaves. You eat cereal in your going-out shirt.

couch.title: Asleep in Your Going-Out Shirt
couch.text: You sat down on the couch for one minute to put on your shoes. It is now 9:40 PM. Your partner is asleep next to you, also in a going-out shirt. The reservation called twice.

legend.title: You Remembered You Like Each Other
legend.text: Dessert. A walk. A whole conversation that wasn't about poop. You get home and the toddler is asleep and the sitter says they were "an angel," which is a lie, but a kind one.

solid.title: A Good Week, Actually
solid.text: Dinner was good. You talked about the toddler for forty-one minutes and each other for twenty. That counts. That absolutely counts.

survived.title: You Made It to Friday
survived.text: You made it to the restaurant, mostly awake. You split an appetizer and a yawn. It wasn't magic. It was a table for two, and that's more than last month.

barely.title: Barely, Together
barely.text: You were home by 8:45 and asleep by 8:50, holding hands, fully dressed. The sitter got paid for three hours. Worth it.

events.title: The Monitor Crackles
events.text: A small voice announces, with total confidence, that it is morning. The sun disagrees. The sun is not in charge here.

choices.label: Go get them. Be the morning person.

outcomes.text: You are greeted like a returning war hero. Then asked for a banana. Then told the banana is wrong.

choices.label: Nudge your partner. It's their turn.

outcomes.text: Your partner gets up without a word. They know the ledger. You get nine more minutes and a dream about sleeping.
"I did it yesterday," your partner mumbles, which is technically true. You get up. The banana is still wrong.
You lie in the dark absorbing nine minutes of escalating demands. Technically rest.

events.title: Breakfast Service
events.text: You cut the toast into triangles. Your toddler wanted squares. Your toddler did not say this out loud. You were supposed to know.

outcomes.text: Squares: approved. One bite is taken. The rest goes into the heating vent.
They consider this. They eat a triangle while making eye contact, like a small mob boss.
The triangle hits the floor butter-side down, as physics demands. So does your toddler.
"Organic Harvest Medley." It costs $3.49 and tastes like a wet garden. They love it.

events.title: Full Meltdown
events.text: Something has gone wrong. Maybe the banana. Maybe the concept of time. Your toddler is a boneless puddle on the floor, screaming at a frequency only dogs and parents can hear.

choices.label: Get on the floor and validate their feelings

outcomes.text: "You're frustrated that the sky is the wrong blue." It works. You are covered in floor dust and something like peace.
The man in corduroy sings about feelings. Your toddler becomes a statue. You drink a coffee while it is still technically hot.

choices.label: Wait it out. Become a rock.

outcomes.text: You become a rock. The storm passes, as storms do. Most last only a few minutes. This one felt like a fiscal quarter.

events.title: The Screen-Off Meltdown
events.text: The credits roll. The silence breaks. This one has a second act, a key change and a lighting design.

outcomes.text: Peace, again. You both know how this ends. You both choose not to think about it.
Twenty minutes of grief for a man in corduroy. Then, abruptly, they want a snack. Like nothing happened. Like you didn't just age.

events.title: Nap Time (Allegedly)
events.text: Your toddler's eyes are drooping. Your toddler is also standing in the crib gripping the bars, yelling "I'M NOT TIRED" like an inmate in a prison movie.

choices.label: Full ritual: sleep sack, white noise, the Song

outcomes.text: They're out. You freeze in the hallway, terrified a floorboard will betray you.
Twenty-two minutes. The shortest nap known to science. They wake up refreshed and furious.

choices.label: Car nap: drive until they pass out

outcomes.text: You drive in circles. They sleep. You sit in the driveway with the engine running, eating crackers from the cup holder. Peak living.
The moment the engine stops, their eyes snap open, like a vampire at sundown.

choices.label: Skip it. They said they're not tired.

outcomes.text: You believe them. This is a mistake. But it's a mistake with an extra hour in it.

events.title: Nap Time: Your 90 Minutes
events.text: They're down. You have about an hour and a half. You have nine hours of things to do.

outcomes.text: You wake with the couch's texture printed on your face. You feel like a new person. A new, slightly damp person.
Every surface is clean. You stand there admiring it. You hear a small voice. It's over.

choices.label: Knock out the oldest thing on your list

outcomes.text: Done. Crossed off. You feel a level of satisfaction usually reserved for people who have slept.
You watch a stranger renovate a bathroom for forty minutes. It's the most relaxing thing you've done since 2019.

events.title: "Who Gave Them the iPad?"
events.text: Your partner walks in, holding the iPad, the toddler and a tone. The iPad is sticky. The toddler is wearing yogurt.

choices.label: "That was me. It was a day."

outcomes.text: They put the iPad down. "Yeah. Mine too." A small truce, signed in yogurt.
It lands. It's true and it doesn't help. Dinner is very quiet.
They read it. They go quiet. Then they take bedtime without being asked. You were right. It still costs something.
They read it. It's not as lopsided as you thought. It's lopsided the other way. You both decide to never mention the ledger again.

events.title: The Handoff
events.text: Your partner walks in. The toddler runs to them like they've returned from war. You've been here all day and you are, apparently, furniture.

choices.label: Tag out. Ten minutes alone in the car.

outcomes.text: You sit in the driveway with the engine off, staring at nothing. It is the best ten minutes of your week.

choices.label: Ask about their day. Really ask.

outcomes.text: They talk. You listen. For six minutes you are two adults having a conversation. The toddler interrupts, but the six minutes happened.
You deliver the full incident report. They nod. They had their own day. Nobody wins the who's-more-tired contest. Nobody ever does.

events.title: The Dinner Standoff
events.text: Dinner contains a vegetable. Your toddler examines the plate like a critic who has already decided to write a bad review.

outcomes.text: A real dinner, with colors. Your toddler eats the bread. You eat the colors. Everyone is fed, technically.
Plain buttered noodles: the official cuisine of toddlerhood. Somewhere, a nutritionist feels a disturbance.
The delivery driver knows your name. The delivery driver knows your toddler's name. This is fine.

events.title: Bedtime: The Final Boss
events.text: It's 7:30. Pajamas are on, after a ten-minute chase. Teeth are brushed: one tooth, briefly. Now comes the negotiation.

choices.label: Full routine: three books, two songs

outcomes.text: Three books become five. Two songs become an encore. But their eyes are closing, and they tell you they love you.
Your partner takes bedtime. You hear the songs through the wall. You lie on the couch, eyes closed, a free person.
"I did it last night." They didn't. You don't have the energy to argue. You do bedtime.
Silence. You don't trust it, so you do the dishes on high alert.
The door clicks shut. A small voice: "I need to tell you something." It's about a dog they saw in April.

events.title: The Early Bedtime
events.text: It's Friday. The sitter comes at 7. The toddler must be asleep by then, which means bedtime is now, which the toddler can smell.

outcomes.text: Warm bath. One book, read at auctioneer speed. One song, abridged. Their eyes go heavy. Yours do too. Not yet.
You do the bath. They do the book. It runs like a pit crew. You high-five in the hallway like idiots.
You both do the bath and neither does the book, and you argue in whispers about whose job the book was.

choices.label: Drive around until they pass out

outcomes.text: Two laps of the neighborhood. Asleep in the car seat. The transfer to the crib is a bomb disposal operation.

events.title: Can You Even Go?
events.text: It's 7:00. The doorbell rings. The reservation is at 7:30. Your going-out shirt has a stain you have decided is a pattern.

outcomes.text: Liquid courage. Your eyes open a little wider. Tonight's sleep will pay for this, but tonight is tonight.
You lie on the bed fully dressed and set three alarms. You wake up confused but upright.
Shoes. Keys. Door. You're out before anyone can ask you for anything.

events.title: Table for Two
events.text: You made it. Candles. Real napkins. Nobody is throwing anything. You both stare at the menu like it's a foreign country.

choices.label: Talk about anything but the toddler

outcomes.text: You last eleven minutes. Then you show each other photos of the toddler. Then your partner says, "Hey. I missed you."
You try. The silences are long. Then you both laugh at the same terrible thing at the next table, and it's almost like before.
Dessert. A second glass. A walk home the long way. You will be destroyed tomorrow. Tomorrow is Saturday.

events.title: Diaper Math
events.text: You open the box. There are four diapers left. You do the math. The math is bad.

outcomes.text: Subscribe and save. Arriving tomorrow. You are an adult who handles things.

choices.label: Text your partner to grab some

outcomes.text: "On it 👍" They will absolutely forget. Wait, no. They send a photo of the receipt. Who is this person?
Read at 2:14 PM. No reply. The diapers remain theoretical.
Four is plenty. Four is a number. Nothing bad has ever happened with four.

events.title: There Are No Diapers
events.text: "Buy diapers" expired. It's evening. There is one diaper left and the toddler has plans for it.

outcomes.text: You buy diapers in slippers under fluorescent lights. The cashier has seen this before. The cashier has seen everything.

choices.label: "Whose turn was it to buy them?"

outcomes.text: It was yours. It was on your list. You both know it. The argument is about something else, as they always are.

events.title: "Did You RSVP?"
events.text: Theo's mom texts the group chat: "Still waiting on a few RSVPs 🙂". The smiley face is doing a lot of work.

outcomes.text: "So sorry!! Crazy week!!" Two exclamation points. The universal sign of a parent drowning politely.

events.title: The Form
events.text: Daycare calls. The form was due this morning. Your child cannot go on the field trip to the pumpkin patch without it, and will be told why.

outcomes.text: You hand-deliver a form like it's a subpoena. The teacher's smile is very patient.

events.title: The Rash, Revisited
events.text: You never called about the rash. The rash has opinions now.

outcomes.text: The nurse is calm and kind and says it's probably eczema. You feel a rush of gratitude so big it's embarrassing.

events.title: Overdue
events.text: The library emails. The books are overdue. One of them is now partially eaten.

choices.label: Pay the fine. Accept your shame.

outcomes.text: $11.40 for a book about a bear who is also tired. You get it, bear.

events.title: It's Quiet. Too Quiet.
events.text: The living room has been silent for six minutes. Silence, in this house, is never good news.

outcomes.text: You catch them uncapping a permanent marker, eyes locked on a fresh white wall. You confiscate it. Crisis averted. This time.
You finish your coffee. It's lovely. It's the last lovely thing for a while.

events.title: The Sharpie Incident
events.text: The hallway is now a mural titled "Untitled (Permanent)."

outcomes.text: Magic eraser, elbow grease, and words you bleep in your head. It's mostly gone. Mostly.
"Our little Basquiat 🎨" Forty likes. One comment asking if it's washable. It is not.

choices.label: Leave it. Deal with it Friday.

outcomes.text: It's a feature wall now. You walk past it eleven times today. It looks at you every time.

events.title: You Said the Word
events.text: Lego, bare foot, 3 PM. You said a word. A [BLEEP] word. Your toddler said it back, perfectly, and is now saying it to the dog. You don't have a dog.

outcomes.text: It will come up again. At daycare. To the director. You know this the way you know the sun will rise.

events.title: The Stomach Bug Has Entered the Chat
events.text: It started with one ominous burp. It ended with you holding a mixing bowl like a goalie. It is coming for you next.

outcomes.text: Every surface, every toy, every doorknob. You smell like a public pool. It might not be enough.
You lay towels like a field medic. The laundry pile reaches a height that requires a permit.

events.title: "You're My Best Friend."
events.text: Out of nowhere, mid-snack, they pat your face with a hand covered in hummus and say it. Then they go back to the snack like nothing happened.

outcomes.text: "!!!!!" they reply, from a meeting. Then a heart. Then: "I'm so jealous."
You don't post it. You don't tell anyone. You just keep it.

events.title: Coffee, Attempt #3
events.text: You've reheated this coffee so many times it's legally a soup.

outcomes.text: You drink it hot. A single tear rolls down your cheek.
A fresh pot. You smell it. You feel briefly human.

choices.label: Skip it. Hydrate like an adult.

outcomes.text: Water. How novel. Your body doesn't know what to do with it.

events.title: A Quiet Moment
events.text: Your toddler is sitting calmly in a corner. When they see you, they say, "I didn't do it." You don't know what "it" is.

outcomes.text: It was the lipstick. It was always going to be the lipstick.

choices.label: Don't ask questions you don't want answered

outcomes.text: You'll find out at 4 PM. It involves the toilet.

events.title: The Crib Whisper
events.text: 2:47 AM. A small figure is standing in the crib whispering your name at the wall. You're about 70% sure this isn't a ghost.

outcomes.text: Twenty minutes of the shush-pat. They go down. You lie awake for forty more, because your body thinks it's a job now.
Your partner gets up without a word. The ledger is a powerful document.
"I got the last two," they whisper. They did. You get up.
The whispering stops. You listen to the silence like it's a symphony.
The whispering becomes yelling. You both get up. Nobody wins.

events.title: You Replay It. Again.
events.text: 3:12 AM. You're replaying the moment you snapped today. In the replay you are calm and wise. In real life you were not.

choices.label: Wake your partner to talk about it

outcomes.text: They listen, half asleep. "You're a good parent," they mumble. "Everyone yells." It helps more than it should. Now you're both awake.

choices.label: Look up how to repair it

outcomes.text: The article says repair matters more than perfection. Tomorrow you'll say sorry. They'll say "OK" and ask for a snack.

events.title: Nothing
events.text: 2 AM, 3 AM, 4 AM. Nothing. The monitor is silent. You wake up every hour anyway, to check that the nothing is still happening.

outcomes.text: You almost don't trust it. Almost.
